correctness.rationale: Reconstructing the dissipator from the off-diagonal jump entries 1±1/√2 gives Bloch rates −1,−2,−3 and z drift 2√2; conjugation swaps x and z. The homogeneous generators add to −4I. Composing the affine translations in physical time gives k(1−v³)(1,0,v) and k(u(1−u⁶),0,(1−u³)(1+u⁵)); dividing by 1−u⁸ gives the displayed fixed states. Independently cross-multiplied and checked all polynomial coefficients in the two purity defects and their strict gap. The regrouped centered polynomial is positive for 0<u<1. In an eigenbasis of the reset state, the nontrivial partial-transpose block has off-diagonal a/2 and determinant (1−a)²δ²/16−a²/4, so the inclusive threshold and integer ceilings hold. Writing C=e^(h D1/2), B=e^(h D2), C²=A gives (CBC)^(m+1)=C(BA)^mBC; EB closure under composition gives the one-cycle upper bound, and the purity ordering gives the lower bound. The boundary defect is tanh²(h/2)(1+2 sech h)/9=h²/12+O(h⁴), and the purity gap is O(h⁴). Multiplying the ceilings by 2h gives the claimed logarithm and O(h) remainder. The pure averaged fixed state has δ=0, so the positive finite-time identity weight never meets the EB criterion.

value.rationale: This quantifies a singular finite-control effect in an existing pure-state stabilization example: every positive dwell gives finite EB while the averaged dynamics never become EB in finite time. The exact phase comparison and logarithmic horizon (including its scale) determine when that operational difference appears, rather than merely showing convergence of the channels at each fixed time.
residual_risks: The finding is for the specified ideal control and equal dwell times; no perturbative robustness or general Floquet law is established.
